_comment: Copy this file to tournament.json and edit it. That is the only file you
need to change to point the whole toolkit at your own tournament.
Your tab username and password do NOT go in here. They go in .env, which
is gitignored — so this file stays safe to commit, screenshot, and paste
into a chat when you are asking somebody for help.
Nothing about your tournament's SHAPE belongs here either. The number of
rounds, which are prelims and which are break rounds, your break
categories and their sizes, how many teams are in a debate, your side
names, your feedback scale and every public/silent switch are all read
off the tab every time a tool runs. If you change them mid-tournament,
the tools follow.

tournament._comment: Only for display. Leave name empty and the pages take it from the tab.

_comment: url  — everything before the tournament name. No trailing slash, no /admin.
e.g. https://yourtournament.calicotab.com
slug — the tournament's own bit of the address, right after the host.
If your tab lives at https://x.calicotab.com/worlds26/ the slug is worlds26.
host — cloudflare (recommended, unmetered bandwidth), netlify, or surge.
The two project names become your public web addresses:
<fold_project>.pages.dev  and  <feedback_project>.pages.dev
Pick something recognisable — people will bookmark it.
port — where the local dashboard listens. Change it only if something
else on your laptop already uses 8790.
Who counts as a tester comes from Tabbycat's own 'adjudication core' flag,
and you can add more people from inside the dashboard.
min_comments — below this, a judge gets a short 'little was written' note
rather than a paragraph of pattern-finding invented from two
lines. Three is a sensible floor.
model        — which Claude model writes the summaries.
concurrency  — how many judges are summarised at once.
